chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Working clubs in Canada and Chicago with Buddy Tate
summary: Back in the States he played Toronto's Colonial Tavern, Blues Alley and London House, often with Buddy Tate.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, so now you are making these periodic trips to Europe and then when you were back in the States where are you working mostly? Are you playing up in .........

Oh, in Canada, I'd say, Toronto. Toronto or Cleveland, at the Theatrical Grill, the Theatrical Restaurant. Mostly Toronto though. I used to stay up in Toronto so much at the Colonial Tavern there. Yes, Canada was next after England.
So, in a sense there are not so many clubs for that type of music now?

No. Not now. Also in Washington you know, at the Blues Alley that's another place I used to play, used to play quite often. But so many of them are changed now. I liked the Colonial Tavern it changed quite a bit. It changed to different types of music.
Also out in Chicago at the London House another place, they still, most of the places still going as they used to.
Now when you went to Toronto and London House what sort of group would you have as a rule. A rhythm section and trumpet or would you have another horn?
No, I'd have, I always took a tenor with me. I took a tenor. Most of the time it was Buddy Tate because Buddy and I had made so many records together. You know, Buck and Buddy, Buck and Buddy Blues.
At the London House I went out there with Ja Jones, when he had a trio. of..
Ray Bryant and Tommy Bryant. But I didn't play with the trio. I did play with
them, but I mean as a special, I only did special numbers. Joe did his thing with the Trio and I'd come on and do it.
